name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Artery Dilatation

criteria.description: Pulmonary artery diameter exceeding 4 cm on imaging without identifiable secondary cause
Exclusion of secondary causes such as pulmonary hypertension, congenital heart disease, or vasculitis
Presence of respiratory symptoms attributable to pulmonary artery dilatation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pulmonary artery diameter >4 cm on imaging with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and exclusion of other etiologies; no standardized formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Isolated pulmonary artery dilatation on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Key diagnostic finding rather than a clinical symptom

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.symptomName: Chest discomfort or retrosternal chest pain
searchTerms: pressure or pain in chest center

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiopulmonary efficiency
searchTerms: fatigue from poor heart and lung function
tiredness due to reduced cardiopulmonary capacity

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

rare.symptomName: Sudden onset chest pain due to pulmonary artery rupture
searchTerms: sudden chest pain from lung artery tear
abrupt chest pain due to lung vessel rupture
sharp chest pain from pulmonary artery break
swelling and fatigue from right heart failure

laboratory: Generally normal laboratory tests; inflammatory markers typically not elevated
Exclusion of infectious or autoimmune causes via serology
imaging: Chest X-ray showing enlarged pulmonary artery silhouette
CT pulmonary angiography demonstrating pulmonary artery diameter >4 cm without thromboembolism
Echocardiography excluding pulmonary hypertension and cardiac anomalies
genetic: No known genetic mutations definitively linked; idiopathic by definition
other: Right heart catheterization to exclude pulmonary hypertension
Pulmonary function tests usually normal or mildly reduced

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated pulmonary artery pressures on right heart catheterization
Secondary pulmonary artery dilatation with clinical signs of pulmonary hypertension
Earlier onset and associated structural cardiac abnormalities
Elevated inflammatory markers and positive autoimmune serology

redFlags: Sudden severe chest pain indicating possible pulmonary artery rupture
Rapidly increasing pulmonary artery diameter on serial imaging
Signs of right heart failure or hemodynamic instability
references: Deterling RA Jr, Clagett OT. Aneurysm of the pulmonary artery; review of the literature and report of a case. Am Heart J. 1947.
Duijnhouwer AL, et al. Pulmonary artery aneurysm: a systematic review. Pulm Circ. 2016.
